messages:
Alex Moran: Heads-up — after pushing OFED 5.8.12 to euc1-nightly last night, we started seeing NCCL allreduce failures and sustained bandwidth drop on several p4d pools this morning. Alerts from perf show ~30% less GB/s for big-reduce workloads. Anyone digging in?
Priya Shah: Seeing the same. EFA reports a lot of QP state changes and rdma_cm reconnect attempts. nccl-tests all_reduce_perf numbers dropped from ~12GB/s to ~8GB/s on affected hosts.
Chen Li: Possible kernel/OFED interaction. We're on kernel 6.4 on these images — OFED 5.8 + 6.4 had a regression with mlx5 SRQ timeout handling in our lab weeks ago. Need to confirm firmware mix.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: rollout of ofed-5.8.12 to euc1-nightly completed at 1945600000 affecting 68 hosts. Monitoring enabled.
Samir Patel: Can someone paste a short log snippet from an affected host? Need error strings to correlate with vendor notes.
Priya Shah: here's a trimmed log from p4d-12:
```
[2026-03-09T07:12:23Z] EFA: qp 0x3f state ERR -> RESET
[2026-03-09T07:12:23Z] rdma_cm: cq error on id 0x7f: -110
NCCL WARN Call to ibv_reg_mr failed: errno 22
NCCL INFO fallback to TCP
```
Alex Moran: Canary comparison: all affected nodes have mlx5 fw 18.16.0. Some unaffected nodes still on 18.12.x. Could be firmware x OFED combo.
Chen Li: Quick checks: run `ethtool -i <iface>` and `ibv_devinfo -v` to confirm driver/firmware combo. Also `ethtool -S <iface>` for counters (port_xmit_discards, port_recv_errors).
Samir Patel: Short mitigation we can apply immediately: set NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1 for the job to force TCP fallback until we fix the stack. Not ideal (latency + throughput hit), but buys time. Example:
```
export NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1
srun -N 8 -n 64 ./build/all_reduce_perf -b 8 -e 512M -f 2 -g 8
```
Priya Shah: Confirmed: TCP fallback restores correctness but perf hits ~40% for cross-node allreduce. For latency-sensitive customers in prod-euc1 this is potentially unacceptable.
Alex Moran: Short-term plan proposal:
- Roll back OFED 5.8.12 on euc1-nightly -> 5.7.x for affected cohort (canary + 2 batches)
- Pin hosts with fw 18.16.0 for now; vendor says 18.16.0 has a risky SRQ change that needs kernel patch
- For critical customers, route traffic to dedicated reserved nodes in other regions/tiers if capacity allows
- Long-term: test matrix for kernel+OFED+firmware combos, add gating in our OFED rollout playbook
Chen Li: Rollback command for ansible run (example):
```
ansible-playbook -i inventory/euc1 hosts_playbooks/rollback_ofed.yml -l 'p4d-nodes-euc1_canary'
```
Samir Patel: Cost/ops note: routing to other regions will spike egress and cross-region costs. If we spin up temporary dedicated capacity in us-west we should estimate ~10% additional hourly spend for the next 48h.
Alex Moran: Who can own the rollback window? We should coordinate a 2h maintenance slot, run validation (nccl-tests + internal QA), then continue roll for rest of fleet if green.
Priya Shah: I can lead the validation tests and pull telemetry dashboards (per-host port counters + NCCL fallback counts). Will post a short checklist when ready.
Chen Li: I'll prepare the rollback playbook changes and a small smoke script to check `ibv_reg_mr` success and no QP ERR loops.
Samir Patel: I'll contact account-ops to draft a brief customer advisory for any impacted latency-sensitive tenants and pre-authorize cross-region burst.
Alex Moran: OK — tentative plan: rollback canary at 1945681800 (in ~45m), validation window 30m, then decide. @Priya Shah @Chen Li @Samir Patel please confirm, add to ops calendar, and post any prechecks here before we start. :thumbsup:
